newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end lower amid electricity concerns.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end lower amid electricity concerns.

text.p: Chilean blue chips closed broadly weaker Friday, with the market dragged down by uncertainty in the electricity sector and concerns that interest rates will not drop until next year, traders said.
The market is expected to show little change next week, although third-quarter results, due to be released by the end of the month, should move individual stocks, said one dealer.
"The market looks flat, but with stocks reacting to company earnings," he said.
The weighted IPSA index ended down 0.45 percent at 100.21 points.
The general IGPA index declined 0.15 percent to 5,447.1 points on volume of 10.2 billion pesos.

Stocks were buffetted by concerns over government plans next month to slash rates on electricity generating and distribution. Jitters over the rate cuts, which could hurt company earnings, are expected to spill over into Monday's opening, traders said.
"The issue of prices will continue upsetting the bolsa's mood next week," said Guillermo Tagle of Santander Investment.
Electricity stocks ended down, with Enersis off 0.61 percent at 243-1/2 pesos.
The market was also depressed by stronger-than-expected economic growth figures this week. The data dashed hopes the central bank would cut interest rates this year.
Telecoms company CTC was the first major company to release third-quarter earnings, and the results exceeded analysts' expectations, Tagle said.
The company said third-quarter net earnings rose to $1.76 per American Depositary Receipt from $1.48 in the same period last year.
Despite the improvement, the company's stock ended off 0.21 percent at 2,450 pesos.
